reference.type: a 20-page vector PDF pitch book (the PDF rendition of a native deck); no template file
reference.notes: No template: blank template at the guide's page size, --chrome draw. Arial is drawn as Liberation Sans, a metric alias, so fit is measurable. The pptx twin in refs/files is the same deck: the judge's panel drops it by hash, and it must not be given as a second reference deck.

brief: Five-page cost diagnostic for a university: cost baseline, spans and layers, procurement, implementation plan, savings bridge.

expected_behavior.statement: Every page of the delivered deck is status fit and the package validates.
expected_behavior.check: deck.build.json: every slides[].status == 'fit'; validation_ok == true; `pptx_tools.py validate --render` ok.

expected_behavior.statement: plan.py check passes on the plan the deck was built with, and the build ran with --plan.
Every figure stated in a title, lead-in or callout is computed from the page's own data.
expected_behavior.check: For each stated figure, recompute it from the brief's data; zero mismatches. The agent's figure-check script is present and passes.

expected_behavior.statement: Every title fits the band above the top rule; a title longer than the reference's longest, and a register the reference writes on under a tenth of its titles, is a warning answered in the report.
expected_behavior.check: deck.build.json: no page refused for its title's lines; each 'title longer than the reference' and 'title register rare in the reference' warning is named in the final report with its reason. The register verdicts (slides[].title.register) and the length verdicts are diagnostics, read beside the blind round, which judges the titles' taste.

expected_behavior.statement: Every exhibit was reasoned out before its spec: the plan carries a brief for it that weighs at least two forms and names the reference's nearest exhibit or why none is near; the render shows what the brief says the reader must see, and the report answers where its marks depart from the reference's. No exhibit is justified by a list of chart types.
expected_behavior.check: plan.py check passes on plan.json; for each exhibit, read its brief and the render: the reader finds reader_must_see without arithmetic and the compared value is drawn (pass or fail). How its marks compare with the reference's digest records (marks, in words) is a diagnostic: each departure is named in the report, and the blind round judges it.

expected_behavior.statement: The section's realised variety is at or above the reference's 10th percentile deck, or each warning is explained as a deliberate parallel.
expected_behavior.check: deck.build.json repetition.warnings empty, or each named in the final report with its reason.

expected_behavior.statement: chart_defaults_taken is empty or every remaining entry is named in the report as intended.
The agent looked at every render and wrote located findings (element id, what, the change), and stayed within the build cap.
expected_behavior.check: Transcript: one findings list per review round; builds <= 8 per 5 pages; the delivered build is the best kept, not merely the last.

expected_behavior.statement: The final report separates measured, completed-by-judgement and substituted values, and lists what the user must supply.
The face stand-in is a metric alias and no page is refused for its font.
expected_behavior.check: preflight.py --reference lists Arial as metric_alias; no 'font refused'.

expected_behavior.statement: Undeclared runs longer than the reference's longest are refused at the plan and declared or removed before the build; where the reference has no run evidence, the corpus's longest run (plan.CORPUS_LONGEST_RUN, 2) stands in, and a repeat it warns about is answered.
expected_behavior.check: plan.check.json refusals empty; any run past the run it is held to (repeats[].held_to and its basis) carries deliberate_parallel; each run warning answered in the plan or the report.
